title: SHAPE-Seq: Multiplexed RNA structure profiling by coupling SHAPE chemistry with high-throughput sequencing
key_innovation: Compared with conventional SHAPE analysis based on capillary electrophoresis, SHAPE-Seq combines SHAPE chemistry with barcoded sequencing libraries, enabling parallel structure probing of multiple RNAs at nucleotide resolution.

ppt_overview.title: How does SHAPE-Seq integrate SHAPE chemistry with sequencing?
ppt_overview.captionTitle: Figure 1. SHAPE-Seq experimental and computational workflow.
ppt_overview.text: A barcode sequence is attached to each RNA molecule, allowing multiple RNAs to be processed simultaneously. SHAPE modifications are converted into sequencing reads, and nucleotide-level reactivities are calculated computationally.

ppt_overview.title: How accurately can SHAPE-Seq reproduce conventional SHAPE measurements?
ppt_overview.alt: Validation of SHAPE-Seq using RNase P RNA
ppt_overview.captionTitle: Figure 2. Validation of SHAPE-Seq using RNase P RNA.
ppt_overview.text: SHAPE-Seq reactivity profiles correlate strongly with conventional SHAPE-capillary electrophoresis measurements and reproduce known RNA structures.

ppt_overview.title: How can SHAPE-Seq analyze multiple RNA variants simultaneously?
ppt_overview.alt: Multiplex RNA structure probing by SHAPE-Seq
ppt_overview.captionTitle: Figure 3. Multiplex RNA structure probing by SHAPE-Seq.
ppt_overview.text: Barcoded SHAPE-Seq libraries enable parallel measurement of structural differences among RNA variants, demonstrating the scalability of sequencing-based SHAPE analysis.

ppt_overview.title: How are SHAPE data incorporated into RNA structure prediction?
ppt_overview.captionTitle: Figure 4. SHAPE-guided RNA secondary structure modeling.
ppt_overview.text: SHAPE reactivities are converted into pseudo-free-energy constraints and incorporated into RNA folding algorithms to improve secondary structure prediction accuracy.
